Neptune :: Bulk properties :: chunk_0009
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Neptune%2C_Earth_size_comparison_true_color.jpg/250px-Neptune%2C_Earth_size_comparison_true_color.jpg)](/wiki/File:Neptune,_Earth_size_comparison_true_color.jpg)

A size comparison of Neptune and Earth

Neptune's mass of 1.024×1026 kg[[8]](#cite_note-fact-10) is intermediate between Earth and the larger [gas giants](/wiki/Gas_giant "Gas giant"): it is 17.15 times that of Earth but just 1/19th [that of Jupiter](/wiki/Jupiter_mass "Jupiter mass").[[g]](#cite_note-mass-85) Its [gravity](/wiki/Gravity "Gravity") at 1 bar is 11.27 m/s2, 1.15 times the [surface gravity](/wiki/Surface_gravity "Surface gravity") of Earth,[[8]](#cite_note-fact-10) and surpassed only by Jupiter.[[79]](#cite_note-Unsöld_&_Baschek_2001-86) Neptune's [equatorial](/wiki/Equator "Equator") radius of 24,764 km[[11]](#cite_note-Seidelmann_Archinal_A'hearn_et_al._2007-13) is nearly four times [that of Earth](/wiki/Earth_radius "Earth radius"). Neptune, like [Uranus](/wiki/Uranus "Uranus"), is an [ice giant](/wiki/Ice_giant "Ice giant"), a subclass of [giant planet](/wiki/Giant_planet "Giant planet"), because they are smaller and have higher concentrations of [volatiles](/wiki/Volatile_(astrogeology) "Volatile (astrogeology)") than Jupiter and Saturn.[[73]](#cite_note-Boss-79) In the search for [exoplanets](/wiki/Exoplanet "Exoplanet"), Neptune has been used as a [metonym](/wiki/Metonymy "Metonymy"): discovered bodies of similar mass are often referred to as "Neptunes",[[80]](#cite_note-87) just as scientists refer to various extrasolar bodies as "Jupiters".

Part of the [Western United States](/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States") region, it is one of the two non-contiguous U.S. states, alongside [Hawaii](/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii"). Alaska is considered to be the northernmost, westernmost, and, longitudinally, the easternmost state in the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States").[[a]](#cite_note-6) It is a [semi-exclave](/wiki/Enclave_and_exclave "Enclave and exclave") of the U.S., bordering the [Canadian territory](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") of [Yukon](/wiki/Yukon "Yukon") and the [province](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") of [British Columbia](/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia") to the east. It shares a western [maritime border](/wiki/Maritime_boundary "Maritime boundary") in the [Bering Strait](/wiki/Bering_Strait "Bering Strait") with [Russia](/wiki/Russia "Russia")'s [Chukotka Autonomous Okrug](/wiki/Chukotka_Autonomous_Okrug "Chukotka Autonomous Okrug"), and is closer to another continent ([Asia](/wiki/Asia "Asia")) than any other U.S. state. The [Chukchi](/wiki/Chukchi_Sea "Chukchi Sea") and [Beaufort](/wiki/Beaufort_Sea "Beaufort Sea") Seas of the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean") lie to the north, and the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") to the south.

Liverpool's third successive League Cup triumph was added through a 2–1 win over [Manchester United](/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") after extra time at Wembley. Rush was voted [PFA Player of the Year](/wiki/PFA_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Player of the Year") and [BBC Wales Sports Personality of the Year](/wiki/BBC_Wales_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "BBC Wales Sports Personality of the Year") in 1984 as Liverpool retained both the League and the League Cup and won the European Cup.[[27]](#cite_note-BBC_1-27)[[28]](#cite_note-28) Rush also added the [Football Writers Footballer of the Year](/wiki/Football_Writers%27_Association_Footballer_of_the_Year "Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year") to the PFA award he had already claimed – the same feat that his strike partner [Kenny Dalglish](/wiki/Kenny_Dalglish "Kenny Dalglish") had achieved a year earlier.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

He scored 47 goals in 65 games (making him the highest goalscorer in all competitions for any professional club that season), a goal every 1.4 matches, as Liverpool finished three points clear of closest rivals [Southampton](/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") in the League. They beat rivals Everton 1–0 in the replayed [final of the League Cup](/wiki/1984_Football_League_Cup_final "1984 Football League Cup final") (after a 0–0 draw in the first ever all-Merseyside final). They also won their fourth European Cup by defeating [AS Roma](/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") 4–2 on penalties in the [final](/wiki/1984_European_Cup_final "1984 European Cup final") following a 1–1 draw after extra time. He also contested the [Intercontinental Cup](/wiki/1984_Intercontinental_Cup "1984 Intercontinental Cup") in Tokyo against [Club Atlético Independiente](/wiki/Club_Atl%C3%A9tico_Independiente "Club Atlético Independiente"), but this time he was on the losing side, defeated by 1–0.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31)

Djibouti's population is predominantly [Muslim](/wiki/Muslim "Muslim"). [Islam](/wiki/Islam "Islam") is observed by around 98% of the nation's population (approximately 891,000 as of 2022).[[241]](#cite_note-244) As of 2012, 94% of the population was Muslim whereas the remaining 6% of residents are Christian adherents.[[1]](#cite_note-CIA-1)

Islam entered the region very early on, as a group of persecuted Muslims had sought refuge across the [Red Sea](/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea") in the [Horn of Africa](/wiki/Horn_of_Africa "Horn of Africa") at the urging of the Islamic prophet [Muhammad](/wiki/Muhammad "Muhammad"). In 1900, during the early part of the colonial era, there were virtually no Christians in the territories, with only about 100–300 followers coming from the schools and orphanages of the few Catholic missions in the [French Somaliland](/wiki/French_Somaliland "French Somaliland"). The Constitution of Djibouti names Islam as the sole [state religion](/wiki/State_religion "State religion"), and also provides for the equality of citizens of all faiths (Article 1) and freedom of religious practice (Article 11).[[180]](#cite_note-English_constitution-183)[[181]](#cite_note-constitution-184) Most local Muslims adhere to the [Sunni](/wiki/Sunni_Islam "Sunni Islam") denomination, following the [Shafi'i](/wiki/Shafi%27i "Shafi'i") school. The [non-denominational Muslims](/wiki/Non-denominational_Muslim "Non-denominational Muslim") largely belong to [Sufi](/wiki/Sufism "Sufism") orders of varying schools.[[242]](#cite_note-245) According to the [International Religious Freedom Report](/wiki/International_Religious_Freedom_Report "International Religious Freedom Report") 2008, while Muslim Djiboutians have the legal right to convert to or marry someone from another faith, converts may encounter negative reactions from their family and clan or from society at large, and they often face pressure to go back to Islam.[[243]](#cite_note-246)

Work on an MCU Spider-Man production began in February 2015.[[107]](#cite_note-108) [Ted Melfi](/wiki/Ted_Melfi "Ted Melfi"), [Jonathan Levine](/wiki/Jonathan_Levine "Jonathan Levine"), and [Jon Watts](/wiki/Jon_Watts "Jon Watts") were among the filmmakers executives considered to direct *Spider-Man: Homecoming*, with Watts ultimately signed as director in June 2015.[[108]](#cite_note-THRCastingSecrets-109) Watts came to Marvel's attention for his work in the independent thriller *[Cop Car](/wiki/Cop_Car_(film) "Cop Car (film)")* (2015).[[109]](#cite_note-iw1-110) The studios hired a succession of writers to produce the script for *Homecoming*.[[110]](#cite_note-SDCC2016-111)[[111]](#cite_note-homecomingew-112) Some 1,500 actors were scouted for the role of [Peter Parker / Spider-Man](/wiki/Peter_Parker_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Peter Parker (Marvel Cinematic Universe)").[[112]](#cite_note-SpideyCastingCall-113) Six of the actors auditioned in screen tests with [Robert Downey Jr.](/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr. "Robert Downey Jr.") in character as [Iron Man / Tony Stark](/wiki/Iron_Man "Iron Man"), which the producers viewed to observe their onscreen chemistry.[[108]](#cite_note-THRCastingSecrets-109)[[112]](#cite_note-SpideyCastingCall-113) The filmmakers held further auditions when [Tom Holland](/wiki/Tom_Holland "Tom Holland") and [Charlie Rowe](/wiki/Charlie_Rowe "Charlie Rowe") were picked as the finalists.[[108]](#cite_note-THRCastingSecrets-109) Holland was cast as Peter in June 2015, signing a six-picture deal to appear in three Spider-Man films and three other MCU films.[[113]](#cite_note-MarvelSonyJune23-114)[[114]]

Fudan University operates four campuses in [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai"): Handan, Fenglin, Zhangjiang and Jiangwan.[[16]](#cite_note-ShanghaiGov_Fudan_2026-16) Handan and Jiangwan serve as the main campus areas, with Fenglin and Zhangjiang as two side campuses.[[17]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily_Govt_Fudan-17) The Handan Road campus is located in [Yangpu District](/wiki/Yangpu_District "Yangpu District").[[18]](#cite_note-QS_Fudan-18) A historical area within the Handan Road campus, known as the Original Site of Fudan University, includes the university history museum, university museum, art museum, science and technology innovation museum, special collections archives and alumni house. The area marks the site where former president [Li Denghui](/wiki/Li_Denghui_(educator) "Li Denghui (educator)") established the original Jiangwan campus in 1922.[[19]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily_Original_Site-19)

The Jiangwan campus includes the Lee Shau Kee Library, which has been used for cultural and public exhibitions, including a 2025 exhibition of works by [Salvador Dalí](/wiki/Salvador_Dal%C3%AD "Salvador Dalí").[[20]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily_Dali_Jiangwan-20) The Fenglin campus is associated with Fudan's medical education and health-science activities, following the merger of Fudan University and Shanghai Medical University in 2000.[[18]](#cite_note-QS_Fudan-18) Zhangjiang campus is located in [Zhangjiang](/wiki/Zhangjiang_Hi-Tech_Park "Zhangjiang Hi-Tech Park"), an area of Shanghai associated with technology and biomedical industries.[[17]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily_Govt_Fudan-17)

Saul Perlmutter :: Work :: chunk_0002
Perlmutter heads the [Supernova Cosmology Project](/wiki/Supernova_Cosmology_Project "Supernova Cosmology Project") at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. It was this team along with the competing [High-z Supernova Search Team](/wiki/High-z_Supernova_Search_Team "High-z Supernova Search Team") led by Riess and Schmidt, which found evidence of the [accelerating expansion of the universe](/wiki/Accelerating_universe "Accelerating universe") based on observing [Type Ia supernova](/wiki/Type_Ia_supernova "Type Ia supernova") in the distant universe. Type Ia supernova occurs whenever a [white dwarf star](/wiki/White_dwarf_star "White dwarf star") gains enough additional mass to pass above the [Chandrasekhar limit](/wiki/Chandrasekhar_limit "Chandrasekhar limit"), usually by stealing additional mass from a [companion star](/wiki/Companion_star "Companion star"). Since all Type Ia supernovae are believed to occur in essentially the same way, they form a [standard candle](/wiki/Standard_candle "Standard candle") whose intrinsic [luminosity](/wiki/Luminosity "Luminosity") can be assumed to be approximately the same in all cases. By measuring the apparent luminosity of the explosion from Earth, researchers can then infer the distance to supernova. Comparing this inferred distance to the apparent [redshift](/wiki/Redshift "Redshift") of the explosion allows the observer to measure both the distance and relative velocity of the supernova.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Saul_Perlmutter_in_2024_at_Berkeley_Lab_02.jpg/250px-Saul_Perlmutter_in_2024_at_Berkeley_Lab_02.jpg)](/wiki/File:Saul_Perlmutter_in_2024_at_Berkeley_Lab_02.jpg)

Perlmutter in 2024

The Supernova Cosmology Project concluded that these distant supernovae were receding more quickly than would be expected due to the [Hubble expansion](/wiki/Hubble_expansion "Hubble expansion") alone, and, by inference, the expansion of the universe must have been accelerated over the billions of years since the supernovae occurred.
